paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when the LORD speaks, what you do with His word matters. He gave Pharaoh a whole day's notice and told him to shelter everything in the field (Exodus 9:18-19). Some of Pharaoh's officials who "feared the word of the LORD hurried to bring their servants and livestock to shelter," while "those who disregarded the word of the LORD left their servants and livestock in the field" (Exodus 9:20-21). Same warning, same day, and two different choices.

Now look at Pharaoh. He says, "This time I have sinned," and even says "The LORD is righteous" (Exodus 9:27). But once the thunder and hail stopped, "he sinned again and hardened his heart" (Exodus 9:34). Moses had told him, "I know that you still do not fear the LORD our God" (Exodus 9:30), and I think that's the lesson, friend: saying the right words is not the same as fearing the LORD.

So why does God go through all this? He tells Pharaoh He raised him up "that I might display My power to you, and that My name might be proclaimed in all the earth" (Exodus 9:16). Moses says the storm will stop "so that you may know that the earth is the LORD’s" (Exodus 9:29), and in Goshen, where the Israelites lived, it did not hail at all (Exodus 9:26). So when God speaks, take Him at His word right away, friend, because there is no one like Him (Exodus 9:14).
